runners_data.name: Arcturus Flame
runners_data.note: Best recent form came over 12-14f on good ground (three places from five similar-going runs), Cieren Fallon is a strong booking and the tailed-headgear (tp) adds focus; 28 days since last run is straightforward, and it is a genuine hold-up horse that needs a strong pace to deliver its finishing kick — the controlled tempo Divot looks likely to set is not ideal.

runners_data.name: Zachary Hickes
runners_data.note: Roger Varian sends out a lightly-raced four-year-old returning after 45 days, stepping up sharply in trip from 10f to 1m3½f for the first time, which is the key unknown; its only similar-going run produced a fourth on good ground, and zero wins or places from three career starts is a concern for handicap purposes even at OR 74.

runners_data.name: Good Onya Mate
runners_data.note: Michael Bell's runner carries a 35-day absence and De Sousa rides, but its pattern of fading in the finish is well-documented; placed once over 14f on good ground, it has been pushed into a midfield map position because the hold-up berths are full — its natural race-style sits at the rear, so it will need to travel wider and earlier than ideal, which historically has not brought out its best.

runners_data.name: Divot
runners_data.note: The sole genuine pace-maker in this field, William Knight's four-year-old arrives 17 days fresh with two recent wins on good ground over 10f — this step up to 1m3½f is the main question, but the uncontested lead and Jamie Spencer's tactical intelligence on a flat, galloping track make this the race's dominant pace influence; STYLE_FIT of 0.94 reflects a slightly out-of-role placement but the role itself (lead) is exactly its natural game.

races.paceDynamic: Divot is the sole confirmed front-runner in a four-horse field and, with no rivals likely to challenge for the lead, Jamie Spencer can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop over this 1m3½f trip on Good to Firm ground at Yarmouth. With Arcturus Flame, Zachary Hickes, and Good Onya Mate all natural hold-up or rear-of-field types, Divot will face zero pressure through the early and middle stages, setting exactly the tempo that suits a horse who has won two of its last five on similar ground. Good Onya Mate has been redistributed to midfield on the map — this field contains more hold-up types than the map can show at the rear, and Good Onya Mate is most likely to find a slightly more forward position than its natural style would suggest, though it is unlikely to seriously pressure Divot for the lead. This race shape overwhelmingly favours a horse that can lead without harassment and build a lead into the straight — the profile of a front-runner who controls the fractions and forces pursuers to find serious late momentum over a trip where Yarmouth's straight run-in offers limited cover.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Divot Leads, Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Divot is allowed to dictate a controlled pace unchallenged and has enough in reserve to withstand any late challenge.
scenarios.body: Divot jumps, takes the rail and settles into an uncontested rhythm; Spencer has petrol in reserve entering the final two furlongs and kicks clear before the closers can organise. With OR 65 and recent course-and-distance winning form on similar going, Divot's low weight and proven front-running ability make this the standout shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Reel In Late
scenarios.trigger: If Divot sets a genuinely fast early tempo and ties up in the closing stages, allowing the hold-up horses to close.
scenarios.body: A strong gallop from Divot burns out in the final furlong, opening a gap for Arcturus Flame, who has placed twice over 14f on good ground and carries the class of Cieren Fallon's experience. Arcturus Flame's recent form over staying trips gives it the profile to mop up a fading leader.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Zachary Hickes Improves
scenarios.trigger: If Roger Varian's runner returns sharper after 45 days off and finds this slower, smaller field to its liking over a stiffer trip.
scenarios.body: Zachary Hickes drops back from 10f to a longer trip where its stamina can be tested, and with Ray Dawson tracking Divot from second, it could sustain a challenge if the pace is genuinely honest. However, its limited recent form (three runs, no win at a comparable level) and a soft-ground blot in its history make this the most speculative shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Good Onya Mate Threatens
scenarios.trigger: If Good Onya Mate, shown in midfield due to redistribution, secures a handy position and its best form over 14f translates here.
scenarios.body: Good Onya Mate has finished second over 14f on good ground and De Sousa may choose to ride it more prominently than its usual role; a pace collapse would suit, but its tendency to fade in the finish and a style-fit discount of 0.93 make this the least likely winning shape. This scenario only materialises if everything else goes wrong for the principals.

watchPoints.text: Divot's stamina at 1m3½f is untested — watch whether Spencer allows any gap between his horse and the field entering the final quarter-mile, as a tiring leader with no pace pressure behind it could be caught.

Arcturus Flame has placed on both its 14f starts on good ground — if Divot does hit a flat spot, Cieren Fallon is the jockey most likely to capitalise quickly and the horse has the trip form to threaten.

Good Onya Mate's redistribution means De Sousa may elect to ride more prominently than usual to avoid being shuffled to the back in a four-runner field — watch the draw and early positioning for any signs it races nearer the pace than its card style suggests.
Zachary Hickes has never raced beyond 10f — monitor paddock behaviour and early race movement for any sign the extra distance is causing the horse to overcook its energy in the opening half-mile.

The going report confirms Good to Firm for this race despite the card listing Good — Yarmouth's fast surface will quicken sectionals in the straight and may expose any stamina limitations in horses dropping back or stepping up dramatically in trip.

races.name: QuinnBet Classified Stakes

runners_data.name: Letsbeatsepsis
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with a sound record on similar Good ground (11 from 15 similar-going runs placed) and racing over 1m for the first time in her string, carrying a 7lb claimer in Jude Fernandes — the solo lead role suits her perfectly here but the step to a mile is a mild unknown.

runners_data.name: Heer's Sadie
runners_data.note: A veteran hold-up performer with place form on Good ground and a capable claimer in Howarth; her true racing style is at the rear of the field, and while the map places her in midfield due to the field's composition, she will likely be doing her best work late when the pace may not be generous enough to suit.

runners_data.name: Keeper Of Secrets
runners_data.note: Consistent but flagged as prone to fading in the finish — the horse's natural style is deep hold-up, and its recent form is built on all-weather surfaces at Southwell rather than turf, making the switch back to Good to Firm ground an additional concern alongside the finish-fade flag.

runners_data.name: Nicely Curved
runners_data.note: Six-year-old whose recent form includes a string of thirds, suggesting she is honest rather than a winner in the making; genuine hold-up profile and Sean Bowen is a noted jockey booking, though her best form has come over shorter with a recent heavy defeat at 2m suggesting the mile here is more appropriate.

runners_data.name: Oh So Audacious
runners_data.note: The most prominent-minded rival to the front-runner across the whole field, racing with an excellent record on Good going (15 from 15 similar-going runs placed); dropping back to 1m from regular 7f assignments is a slight query but the prominent style could see her slot just behind Letsbeatsepsis in a race with little other pace.

runners_data.name: Castlekeely
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with a 70-day absence, a flagged tendency to fade in the finish, and a modest record on Good ground (0 wins, 0 places from 4 similar runs); Cieren Fallon is a positive, but the hold-up style and lack of recent racing make this a speculative runner.

runners_data.name: Dee's Honey
runners_data.note: Lightly raced three-year-old back after a lengthy 155-day break, which is a significant fitness flag; the horse's natural instinct is to race at the back, and with limited turf form and a fade tendency, the layoff makes it hard to see her producing a peak effort here.

runners_data.name: El Carrusel
runners_data.note: Three-year-old whose recent form at Yarmouth over 7f suggests he handles the track, and John Ryan's horses can improve sharply with experience; instinctively a hold-up type pushed into a midfield map position, so his finishing run will depend on the pace being genuine enough to reel in those ahead.

runners_data.name: Lordsbridge Bay
runners_data.note: Another three-year-old with a poor placed record on Good ground (0 from 8 similar-going runs), racing out of a hold-up shape and fitted with blinkers; Silvestre De Sousa is the standout booking in the race and could extract more than the form figures suggest, though the overall profile is uninspiring.

runners_data.name: Poetic Grace
runners_data.note: Placed at three runs ago on Good ground over 7f but bred for further; blinkers applied, natural hold-up style pushed into midfield by the map's redistribution, and Conrad Allen's yard (1 from 4 in last 14 days) is quiet — finishing late will require a sharper tempo than this race shape appears likely to produce.

races.paceDynamic: Letsbeatsepsis is the sole confirmed front-runner in a field of ten and, with no genuine challenger disputing for the lead, she is set to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the outset on Good to Firm ground at Yarmouth's flat mile. Oh So Audacious is the one horse with a prominent style who could press for position early, but the remainder of the field — Heer's Sadie, Keeper Of Secrets, El Carrusel, Dee's Honey, and Poetic Grace — are true hold-up types who have been redistributed in the map because the field contains far more closers than genuine pace-setters, meaning Letsbeatsepsis is unlikely to be seriously tested for the lead. With one horse able to control tempo from the front, a falsely steady early pace is the most probable scenario, which sets up a strong-run final two furlongs where horses that can travel prominently and quicken off an honest clip hold a clear advantage over deep closers who need a truly searching gallop to deliver their finishing kick. This race shape most directly favours horses that can sit just off the pace and have the tactical speed to respond when the tempo lifts — a prominent-to-midfield profile that avoids both the energy cost of leading alone and the risk of being left flat-footed by a lack of pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Letsbeatsepsis Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Letsbeatsepsis is allowed to bowl along unchallenged and sets a measured, even tempo that suits a prominent racer quickening off a steady pace.
scenarios.body: Letsbeatsepsis dictates every yard of the race, her main rivals forced to challenge wide or time their run from midfield, and the absence of genuine pressure means she conserves enough energy to repel late challengers on the flat Yarmouth straight. Oh So Audacious, best positioned to race prominently behind her, is the most natural beneficiary if Letsbeatsepsis falters, while Nicely Curved's hold-up style could threaten if she produces a clean late run.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Reel In Solo Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Letsbeatsepsis's solo lead proves costly in the final two furlongs and the hold-up horses that managed to settle produce a stronger finishing effort than the easy pace warranted.
scenarios.body: A modest early gallop paradoxically leaves Letsbeatsepsis vulnerable in the final furlong as she ties up, and horses like Heer's Sadie or Nicely Curved, who have the natural ability to finish off a mile, arrive in time. However, this scenario is genuinely discounted because most of the closers are redistributed hold-up types whose ability to produce a true finishing burst behind a slow pace is uncertain.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Fight It Out
scenarios.trigger: If Oh So Audacious moves to press Letsbeatsepsis before halfway, injecting enough pace to create a genuine contest between the two prominent types.
scenarios.body: The added pressure lifts the tempo into a genuinely run race, meaning the front two fight out a proper duel and those furthest back may find the distance insufficient to peg them back in time. Oh So Audacious's strong prominent profile at this sort of trip and going is well suited, and Letsbeatsepsis could still find enough to hold on if her fitness is sharp.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Field Bunches
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo is so slow that the race becomes a sprint from two furlongs out and tactical speed from any position proves decisive.
scenarios.body: With the field compressed, horses with any pace whatsoever can make ground from almost anywhere, and the race degenerates into a lottery that strips edge from the true front-runner and true closer alike. This outcome is the least likely given Letsbeatsepsis's known willingness to bowl along, but it cannot be entirely dismissed in a low-grade classified stakes.

watchPoints.text: Letsbeatsepsis is unopposed on the front end — watch if jockey Jude Fernandes (7lb claimer) allows her to coast at a dangerously slow tempo, which could bring the entire field within striking range at the two-furlong pole.

Oh So Audacious is the one prominent-style horse capable of pressing Letsbeatsepsis; if Jack Mitchell decides to challenge for the lead early, the resulting pace injection fundamentally changes the race shape and the probability of Scenario C rises sharply.

Lordsbridge Bay with Silvestre De Sousa is a significant jockey upgrade in a field of mostly claiming or smaller-profile riders — watch for De Sousa to produce a tactically smart ride that overrides the horse's moderate recent form figures.

Multiple redistributed hold-up horses (Heer's Sadie, El Carrusel, Dee's Honey, Poetic Grace) will all be seeking the same ground late in the straight — congestion and lack of clear runs in the final furlong is a genuine risk in a 10-runner field where most runners want to finish late.

Dee's Honey returns from 155 days off and is the runner most likely to need the race — if she is given a quiet educational outing rather than a full competitive ride by Darragh Keenan, her finishing effort should be treated as a reference run rather than a genuine threat.

races.name: QuinnBet Best Odds Guaranteed Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Lazzar
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a 4th on Good at 5f last time; apprentice jockey Christian Howarth takes 3lb off, which helps at the weights, but the form string (0-6-9-4-2-4) suggests he finds winning difficult and sim-going record (0 wins from 15) gives no confidence on this surface.

runners_data.name: Creative Queen
runners_data.note: Haggas's runner has strong handler form (6/47 in 14 days) and Cieren Fallon is a significant booking; wears a hood, broke the ice to win at 6f on Soft but sim-going record at Good is modest (0W/2P from 7), and dropping to 5f could sharpen her — though her front-running role means she must contend with two rivals for the lead.

runners_data.name: London Is Blue
runners_data.note: Won over 6f on Good last time out and has a pair of course wins, but the hold-up style means London Is Blue needs the pace to collapse in a short 5f; fitted with a visor and the Cowell stable is ticking over quietly (1/9 in 14 days), so the positional disadvantage is the key factor to weigh.

runners_data.name: Zoustar Dreams
runners_data.note: Has won twice at 5f on Good/Soft and is the most proven front-runner in the field over this exact trip; Jamie Spencer is an astute pilot who can gauge pace, and the Ed Dunlop yard has a live runner (1/17 T14) — if she leads uncontested, her record suggests she is very hard to peg back.

runners_data.name: Cameley Days
runners_data.note: Silvestre De Sousa takes a prominent position on a horse that has won twice at 5f on Good ground; the Chris Dwyer yard is quiet (0/4 T14) and the recent form includes a disappointing 0 last time, but in a strong-pace scenario, sitting just off the speed suits the way he has won before.

runners_data.name: Rumble Ruby
runners_data.note: Won two days ago (LR: 2d) which is a notable freshness flag to monitor — but the record at 5f on Good is strong (1W/2P from 3), and the prominent-to-hold-up style means Rumble Ruby can sit just off the contested lead and pounce; the 5lb apprentice claim from Liam Wright aids the weights.

runners_data.name: Always Perfect
runners_data.note: Tailed-on tongue strap and front-running style means Always Perfect goes into direct competition with two rivals for the early lead; has won and placed at 6f on Good but dropping to 5f with a contested gallop is a stiff ask, and Paddy Bradley is a less experienced booking here.

runners_data.name: Sunlit Sea
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's yard is firing (5/27 T14) and Sunlit Sea has won twice at 5f on Good recently; wears a hood and is held up, which maps well to a pace-collapse scenario — the 7lb apprentice Poppy Scott takes the ride, which is a significant weight advantage that makes the hold-up style easier to carry off.

races.paceDynamic: Creative Queen, Zoustar Dreams, and Always Perfect are all confirmed front-runners in a field of just eight over Yarmouth's sharp, flat 5f, guaranteeing a genuinely strong early gallop from the off. With three horses intent on leading, there will be immediate competition for the rail and the front rank, meaning the pace is unlikely to be stolen — it will be contested hard, burning energy from the first stride. The fast-ground conditions (Good to Firm confirmed for this race) will amplify the speed of early sectionals, placing a premium on those who can sustain their effort rather than those who need to build into it. This race shape strongly favours prominent-to-hold-up profiles — specifically horses like Rumble Ruby and Sunlit Sea who have proven ability at 5f on Good or faster ground, can sit just off a franked pace, and finish with purpose once the front-runners tie each other up in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Creative Queen, Zoustar Dreams, and Always Perfect burn each other out fighting for the lead, setting up the race for those tracking just off the pace.
scenarios.body: The three front-runners push hard from the gates, creating a truly run 5f that saps the leaders' reserves in the final furlong; hold-up and prominent horses who have settled just behind the battle are gifted a clear run with momentum.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Leader Controls Race
scenarios.trigger: If one of the three front-runners breaks sharply and establishes an uncontested lead, dictating terms at a sustainable clip.
scenarios.body: Without the early pace duel, the leader gets a softer gallop and is able to find extra when challenged; Zoustar Dreams has the best front-running form at this trip and on this ground, making her the likeliest beneficiary if rivals miss the break.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Horses Score
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong but not catastrophic, and a horse tracking the leaders in second or third converts positional advantage into a late surge.
scenarios.body: Lazzar and Cameley Days sit close enough to the speed to control their own destiny without burning out early, and on Good to Firm at Yarmouth's flat 5f a prominent position with a strong finishing kick can be decisive.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly suicidal and the entire front rank collapses, allowing the deepest-held runners to mow down a field of tiring leaders.
scenarios.body: London Is Blue and Sunlit Sea are the furthest back and would need an unusually messy, burning gallop to deliver their best from off the pace; Yarmouth's flat 5f offers limited run-in for a pure late charge, making this a lower-probability outcome.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Creative Queen, Zoustar Dreams, or Always Perfect breaks fastest — whoever leads uncontested changes the entire shape of the race and lifts Scenario B probability sharply.

Rumble Ruby ran just two days ago; if there is any sign of a sluggish or flat break in the early strides, the short-recovery risk is real and could neutralise what looks an otherwise ideal pace-scenario profile.

Sunlit Sea's yard form is the strongest in the race (Prescott 5/27 in 14 days) and the weight relief from Poppy Scott's 7lb claim is meaningful — if the pace truly combusts, this hold-up runner is the likeliest late swooper to threaten.

London Is Blue wears a visor and has course form, but needs a fully strung-out pace at a sharp 5f to get competitive from a hold-up position — watch for whether the horse is travelling smoothly early, as any traffic trouble at Yarmouth's tight track will end the chance immediately.

The Good to Firm confirmation (not mere Good) across the card tightens the ground outlook — horses with proven winning form on Fast/Firm, specifically Zoustar Dreams and Sunlit Sea, hold a subtle but real edge over those who have only placed on such conditions.

races.name: Danny Frost - Medlock Electrical Distributors Classified Stakes

runners_data.name: Bullington Bry
runners_data.note: Redistributed to the lead by default — a natural hold-up horse forced into the role of pace-setter, which is a significant concern; OR 49, trainer Jessica Macey has had a quiet 14-day spell (0/3), and sim-going form is modest (0W1P from 15 runs), so confidence in it sustaining any real gallop is low.

runners_data.name: Mister Sandman
runners_data.note: Solid recent form (2-3-4 finishes) on Good ground at 6f suits this course and going well; hold-up style naturally suits a race with a soft pace if gaps open, and Jude Fernandes's 7lb claim offers useful weight relief — 66 days off is worth monitoring but the form profile is consistent.

runners_data.name: My Mate Beattie
runners_data.note: Races hold-up but the map places her forward due to congestion at the rear; Scott Dixon's yard has been ticking over (1/11 in 14 days) and recent turf form at 6f on Good ground showed a place (3rd), though a string of disappointing runs on Tapeta raises questions about consistency.

runners_data.name: Payforanother Daay
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up operator shuffled into midfield on the map — most recent form figures (6-0-5-7-5) are uninspiring and sim-going turf form (0W2P) is moderate; at OR 43, lowest in the field, improvement needed and headgear (blinkers) is a notable flag.

runners_data.name: Thanks Dad
runners_data.note: Television visor-wearing hold-up type who maps to midfield simply due to runner congestion; a run of double-figure finishes on turf (10th, 13th, 10th) is a serious concern and 48 days off adds risk — hard to see this finding a way into the argument.

runners_data.name: Valadero
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on Good and placed at 6f on Good — the most relevant sim-going form of any runner here (1W4P from 15 runs); LR of just 8 days suggests fitness, Brian Toomey's yard is in decent form (2/6 in 14 days), and a hold-up profile that can sit closer than rivals is a genuine tactical asset.

runners_data.name: Mayflower Rock
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with limited experience (5 runs) — best form came when third on Good at 5f, and the step up to 6f on Yarmouth's straight track is unproven; true hold-up style pushed forward by the map, so treat its midfield position as misleading and Stevie Donohoe will need to manage positioning carefully.

runners_data.name: My Mate Mackley
runners_data.note: Consistent form string (1-2-2-2-4) shows a horse that competes at the sharp end, but it is a natural hold-up type placed in midfield on the map because the rear is overcrowded; OR 47 and a 7lb claimer (Oliver Carmichael) keeps costs down, and sim-going form (0W2P) is competitive enough to feature.

runners_data.name: Red Legs
runners_data.note: Lightly raced three-year-old with just three runs — placed fourth at 5f on Good and opened at 8/6f on heavier ground, making this trip and conditions relatively unexplored; Silvestre De Sousa is the class jockey booking in the race and that alone keeps interest, but the form book offers little to hang confidence on.

races.paceDynamic: Bullington Bry is the lone confirmed pace-setter here, redistributed to the front despite a natural hold-up profile, meaning the early gallop will be set by a horse racing out of role — likely resulting in a steady, uncontested tempo on this flat Yarmouth 6f. The vast majority of the field are genuine hold-up or come-from-behind types, with Mister Sandman, Valadero, Red Legs and others all likely to settle in behind whatever modest pace is set. This field holds far more hold-up runners than the race shape can accommodate at the rear — Mayflower Rock, My Mate Mackley, My Mate Beattie, Thanks Dad and Payforanother Daay are all genuine hold-up types shuffled forward on the map simply because there is no room; in reality, Valadero and Mister Sandman, both with proven form on Good ground at this trip, are most likely to secure the prominent positions behind the solo leader. A soft, controlled tempo on a flat, fair track with a wall of closers unable to all get their ground favours the horse who can travel prominently in second or third and produce a sustained finish — the prominent racer who can sit just off the pace and quicken on Good to Firm ground holds the clear positional advantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Bullington Bry sets a soft, uncontested pace and the closers face a wall of traffic in the straight, the horse sitting closest in second or third can kick clear.
scenarios.body: A steady tempo on a flat track means the lead is cheap and the prominent slot is gold — whoever travels smoothly just off Bullington Bry faces minimal pressure and can sprint from two out with a clean run.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If two runners manage to press Bullington Bry and create a genuine contest for the lead, the pace quickens and closers struggle to pick them off.
scenarios.body: A genuine dual between early leaders on a flat, straight track burns off the true hold-up runners who need a stronger pace to close into — the horse that controls from the front two emerges with a fitness advantage.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Sweep Home
scenarios.trigger: If Bullington Bry sets a genuinely strong pace and the field spreads wide, allowing hold-up horses a clear run through on the stands side.
scenarios.body: A fast early gallop on Good to Firm ground stretches the field and leaves the true hold-up runners with daylight to close — horses who can produce a sustained late run from off the pace benefit most in this shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Scrappy Blanket Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses mid-race and the field concertinas, turning the race into a sprint from the two-furlong pole with no clear tactical advantage.
scenarios.body: Congestion in a slow-run sprint-finish plays into the hands of the highest-OR runners with the most class, and any horse drawn to find a clear passage first claims a crucial edge.

watchPoints.text: Bullington Bry is a hold-up horse forced onto the lead — if it fades rapidly from the two-furlong marker, any runner caught behind it without a clear path faces a sudden traffic problem.

Valadero's jockey Liam Wright (5lb claimer) must judge pace from a prominent position in what could be a slowly-run race — mistiming the challenge by going too early or too late on a flat track is a real risk.

With Mayflower Rock, My Mate Mackley, My Mate Beattie, Thanks Dad and Payforanother Daay all true hold-up types jostling for position in a small nine-runner field, overcrowding on the rail or through the middle could create interference in the final two furlongs — watch for shuffling in running.

Red Legs holds the strongest jockey booking with Silvestre De Sousa in the saddle — any market move in the final hour before post time should be taken seriously given the booking's implied stable confidence for a lightly raced three-year-old.

Going is reported Good to Firm for the 5:00 race specifically — any late watering or drying will compress finishing times and increasingly favour horses proven on quick ground, of which Valadero and Mister Sandman have the clearest credentials.
